text: The 'von Neumann bottleneck,' which neuromorphic computing aims to overcome, is:
choices: The maximum clock speed achievable by silicon transistors
The energy dissipated as heat each time a transistor switches
The limit on how many neurons can be simulated in software at once
The throughput limitation created by separating memory from processing, forcing data across a bus for every operation
explanation: In the von Neumann architecture, memory and processing are physically separated, so data must traverse a bus for each operation. Biological computation co-locates memory and processing (synaptic weights, molecular state), which is why neuromorphic designs pursue co-located memory-and-compute, spiking dynamics, and local learning. The bottleneck is about the memory-processing split, not clock speed, switching heat, or simulation scale.
